source: Arcadis for Canal & River Trust, Caen Hill Pumping Station Pump Audit Summary Report, 2020 (Interreg Green WIN public deliverable)
question: Audit the Caen Hill pumping station. The operator reports short bearing and seal life, gasket failures and higher than expected energy use. Using the site tests, SCADA data and system description, diagnose the causes (hydraulic, vibration, surge, control), quantify any unexplained losses with the simulator, and recommend measures with their expected benefit.

collection.question: Audit the Caen Hill pumping station. The operator reports short bearing and seal life, gasket failures and higher than expected energy use. Using the site tests, SCADA data and system description, diagnose the causes (hydraulic, vibration, surge, control), quantify any unexplained losses with the simulator, and recommend measures with their expected benefit.

rfi.issue: Duty configuration conflict: Table 1 says Duty/Assist (p.7) but Section 6 says both pumps operate in parallel duty/duty fixed 48 Hz (p.13). Which is design vs normal?
rfi.reason: Affects firm capacity definition, POR assessment and energy comparison; need stated normal to assess 2-pump left-of-POR operation
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Normal operation is both pumps parallel at 48 Hz (duty/duty) with single-pump as fallback; Table 1 Duty/Assist describes installed standby capability. Reason: explicit Section 6 operating description and all 2-pump tests (p.13, p.12, p.16).

rfi.issue: Intermediate NRVs effectiveness unknown; surge result depends on open vs working (p.7, p.19). No inspection due to concrete covers.
rfi.reason: Determines whether 17.5-20 bar.g peaks apply; cannot conclude gasket/surge risk without bounding
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Assess both bounds, adopt NRVs open (failed) as conservative base for surge diagnosis. Reason: report highlights high transients assuming NRVs not operational (p.19).

rfi.issue: Pipe/fitting pressure rating, gasket rating, and allowable surge not stated; 13-20 bar.g cannot be judged (p.19) vs flange leaks (p.8, p.18).
rfi.reason: Needed to judge non-conformance and damage risk from slam/trip peaks
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Treat tabulated 13-20 bar.g as high and potentially damaging given observed gasket failures, pending rating confirmation. Reason: report calls them high/excessive and links ball checks to slam (p.18-p.19).

rfi.issue: Head-loss coefficient 120 units and roughness/elevation inputs not fully dimensioned; Figure 6 calculation sheet not legible as text (p.11, p.9). Orifice 224 mm equivalence given (p.11).
rfi.reason: Cannot replicate unexplained 6 m at 300 l/s loss without inputs; simulator must quantify
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Model rising main 3602 m x 600 mm DI with 72 m static (55.5 to 127.6 mAOD context) and calibrate added loss to reproduce +6 m at 300 l/s (≈ orifice 224 mm). Reason: explicit p.11 quantification provides calibration target.

rfi.issue: Bellmouth diameter D, exact clearance, wet-well dimensions, operating levels range, and suction/discharge pressure readings not tabulated; only pump centre 54.3 and well 55.5 mAOD (p.7) and qualitative conformance (p.19).
rfi.reason: Cannot verify ANSI/HI 0.3D-0.5D or NPSHa/submergence numerically
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Accept report qualitative findings (no submergence issue; clearance too high; large wide well prone to deposition; 30% screen loss; 40 t debris) as facts for diagnosis. Reason: direct observations Aug 2019 (p.19).

rfi.issue: Manufacturer Q-H curve only as figure (Fig 8 p.14) with BEP points 262 l/s @70 m / 524 l/s @70 m (p.11); 0.3 Hz derate noted (p.11) but full curve points not listed.
rfi.reason: Needed for POR (70-120% BEP) and wire-to-water simulation
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Use stated BEPs and 50/48/45 Hz test flows (118-310 l/s) with 0.3 Hz derate to represent curves; anchor simulation to measured duties. Reason: only numeric curve data available (p.11-p.12).

rfi.issue: Vibration acceptance for 2-vane pump technically outside WIMES definitions (p.16); truncated 3-or-5-diameter NRV spacing rule (p.18); specific-energy header truncated kWh/100 0 m3 (p.12); Table 5 referenced but Table 3 shown (p.13).
rfi.reason: Need consistent limit and avoid mis-citing energy table
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Apply 11.2 mm/s RMS as acceptance limit; cite energy as Table 3; note NRV spacing criterion incomplete so rely on slam + untied adaptors + bracing observation. Reason: report explicitly recommends 11.2 (p.16) and describes slam/untied/bracing (p.18-p.19).

rfi.issue: SCADA pressures, daily volumes (Fig 7 graph only p.13), flowmeter calibration, VSD/drive efficiencies, and plinth-to-floor anchorage detail (could not be seen p.17) not quantified.
rfi.reason: Affects loss attribution, energy and vibration root-cause certainty
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Treat SCADA as corroborating site tests (p.11); flowmeter as correct for test comparison; plinths as poorly anchored per most-likely-cause finding and touch-test difference (p.17-p.18). Reason: report conclusions based on same inputs.

alternatives.cost_basis: No hardware; telemetry setpoint + operating instruction change only (ASSUMPTION: labour only, based on existing VSD + SCADA p.7 p.13)
alternatives.option: Normal single-pump duty/assist at 48 Hz instead of fixed duty/duty
alternatives.result: TRY-A-1P48: 171.7 l/s at 194.6 kW, TDH 76.85 m vs BASE-CAL 2-pump: 259.8 l/s at 316.7 kW; moves each running pump from ~133 l/s (~51% BEP, outside POR p.11 p.14 p.16) to ~172 l/s inside POR; measured specific energy 296-310 (1-pump) vs 347.6 (2-pump) kWh/1000m3 (p.12)

alternatives.cost_basis: CCTV/pressure survey + lift concrete covers at remote towpath NRVs + clean/flush (p.7); ASSUMPTION: survey + minor remedial, no main replacement
alternatives.option: Investigate and remove 6 m at 300 l/s restriction + prove intermediate NRVs
alternatives.result: ALT-1P48-CLEAN (minor_k 20 ASSUMPTION: clean main): 181.8 l/s vs TRY-A-1P48 fouled 171.7 l/s (+10.1 l/s); ALT-2P48-CLEAN: 299.3 l/s vs TRY-A-2P48 259.8 l/s (+39.5 l/s); calibrates p.11 6 m loss = orifice 224 mm (velocity 7.613 m/s vs 1.061 m/s in 600 mm); TDH falls 76.85 to 75.3 m (1-pump)

alternatives.cost_basis: Regular clean already required after 40 t removal (p.19); benching civils in large well (p.19-p.20); ASSUMPTION: clean opex + minor civils
alternatives.option: Scheduled wet-well/screen cleaning + benching review (retain debris buffer)
alternatives.result: No steady-state head change modelled; protects 4 m NPSH margin (p.12) and prevents skewed/air-entrained inflow from 30% screen loss (p.19); addresses cavitation pitting despite NPSHa sufficiency and 121 to 169 l/s blockage recovery (p.11); supports ALT flows above

alternatives.cost_basis: Exchange 2x 300 mm ball checks (p.7 p.18) for slow-closing, tie adaptors, re-anchor plinths/motor support (p.17-p.19); ASSUMPTION: station pipework retrofit, no main works
alternatives.option: Replace ball checks, tie manifold, re-anchor pumps/plinths; retain 30 s ramp
alternatives.result: Steady state unchanged (BASE-CAL manifold 8.22 bar); targets VariSim peaks 17.5 bar.g (2-pump trip), 20 bar.g (1-pump trip), 13 bar.g (30 s ramp) (p.19) and slam from ball valves (p.18) linked to gasket failures (p.18); targets >11.2 mm/s vibration all duties (p.16) and 2000-3000 h vs 50000 h bearing life (p.14); plinth-floor touch difference and unsupported motor (p.17) support anchoring cause

alternatives.cost_basis: Use existing EM meter (p.13) + SCADA + Mitsubishi VSDs (p.7); ASSUMPTION: controls integration only
alternatives.option: Flow/level-based alternating VSD control with 30 s ramp, keep 48 Hz sweet-spot
alternatives.result: ALT-1P50-1P: 206.8 l/s at 240.7 kW (323.3 kWh/ML) vs TRY-A-1P48 171.7 l/s; 48 Hz lowest specific energy vs 50/45 Hz (p.13) and 45 Hz duties 118 l/s single /191 l/s dual (p.12) with TRY-A-2P45 166.3 l/s showing low-speed inefficiency; avoids fixed duty/duty (p.13) and enables standby rotation

issues.evidence: Rerun BASE-CAL matches logged: 259.8 l/s total, 129.9 l/s per pump, TDH 82.64 m, manifold 8.22 bar, 316.7 kW. Rerun TRY-A-1P48 matches: 171.7 l/s, TDH 76.85 m, 194.6 kW. Study uses low BASE-CAL for benefit comparison, understating 2-pump energy vs measured 333.5 kW. Energy benefit of single-pump therefore uncertain by ~30 kW (~9%).

issues.evidence: p.11 gives no C-factor or curve points; p.9 says roughness based on site measurements but no value. issues.evidence: p.7: station pipework 300 mm, ball NRVs, untied adaptors; p.11: minor_k 120 needed to match SCADA, +6 m at 300 l/s = orifice 224 mm. issues.issue: Unexplained loss misattributed to fouled rising main. Station 300 mm branches, manifold, meter, valves not modelled separately.
